questions.q: In a polling unit in Aba, a voter marks the ballot paper inside a screened booth and drops it into a sealed ballot box. The main purpose of this arrangement is to
options: preserve the secrecy of the voter’s choice
enable the electoral officer to change votes after polling
allow party agents to inspect each ballot before counting
make it compulsory for voters to declare their choices publicly
questions.explanation: A screened booth and sealed ballot box are meant to keep the ballot secret and protect the voter from intimidation. Agents inspecting ballots or voters declaring choices publicly would defeat that purpose.

questions.q: Which of the following best describes a free and fair election?
options: An election in which the ruling party wins all available seats
An election in which voters are required to vote for the candidate approved by traditional rulers
An election in which only people with property can cast their votes
An election conducted by an impartial body, with a credible register and equal opportunity for candidates to campaign
questions.explanation: A free and fair election requires an impartial electoral body, a credible register and a level playing field for candidates. Making only property owners eligible or allowing traditional rulers to direct voters would restrict choice and fairness.

questions.q: Nigeria maintains high commissions in some Commonwealth countries and embassies in others mainly to
options: supervise the internal elections of the host countries
train the armed forces of the host countries
promote and protect her national interests in the host countries
collect taxes from all Nigerians resident abroad
questions.explanation: Diplomatic missions promote and protect Nigeria’s interests, including the welfare of citizens and trade relations. They do not normally collect taxes from all Nigerians abroad or supervise host-country elections.

questions.q: A written constitution is said to be rigid when
options: it is contained in several documents and conventions
it can be amended only through a special procedure involving more than the ordinary legislative majority
it is made by a military government without ratification
it cannot be amended under any circumstances
questions.explanation: Rigidity refers to a special amendment process involving a larger majority or additional approvals. Such a constitution can still be amended; being written in several documents or being made without ratification does not define rigidity.

questions.q: The aspect of sovereignty which refers to a state's freedom from control by another state in its external relations is called
questions.explanation: External sovereignty means that a state is independent of external control in its relations with other states. Internal sovereignty, by contrast, concerns supreme authority over persons and groups within the state's own territory.

questions.q: Mrs Adeyemi directs her child to prepare for school, and the child complies because she accepts that her mother has the right to give such an instruction. This best illustrates
questions.explanation: Authority is power that is accepted as rightful by those subject to it. The child obeys because she recognises the parent's right to direct her, not merely because of force or persuasion.

questions.q: The main function of public opinion in a democracy is to
options: determine the outcome of every court case
guide the government in making policies and decisions
remove the need for periodic elections
replace the work of the judiciary
questions.explanation: Public opinion provides feedback to government and helps shape policies and decisions. It does not replace the courts or elections, which are separate institutions and processes in a democracy.

questions.q: The Pan-African Parliament of the African Union is best described as
options: a consultative body with advisory and limited legislative functions
the military peacekeeping arm of the African Union
the body that elects the Chairperson of the African Union Commission
the highest court of the African Union
questions.explanation: The Pan-African Parliament was created to provide a platform for African peoples and to advise AU organs; it does not have full law-making powers. Judicial, peacekeeping and commission leadership functions belong to other AU institutions.

questions.topic: Separation of powers and checks and balances
questions.q: In Lagos State, the House of Assembly refuses to approve the governor’s request to borrow ₦20 billion until the Commissioner for Finance appears before it to explain the proposal. This action best illustrates
options: exercise of the prerogative of mercy
questions.explanation: The legislature is checking the executive’s financial plans by demanding accountability before approval. This is oversight, not a court review, a transfer of law-making power, or a mercy power.

questions.q: The principal responsibility for formulating and executing Nigeria’s foreign policy lies with the
options: Federal Ministry of Foreign Affairs under the President
National Assembly Committee on Foreign Affairs
questions.explanation: Foreign policy is initiated and executed mainly by the executive through the Ministry of Foreign Affairs, coordinated by the President. The legislature and courts may have related roles, but they do not formulate and execute foreign policy day to day.

questions.q: A coalition of civil society organisations deploys trained observers to polling units in Enugu State during a governorship election. Their main contribution to the electoral process is to
options: declare the winner of the election
enhance transparency and public confidence in the results
questions.explanation: Observers monitor and report on the conduct of voting and counting, which promotes transparency and confidence. They do not possess legal power to declare results, register voters, or draw constituency boundaries.

questions.q: Which of the following items is on the Exclusive Legislative List under the 1999 Constitution of Nigeria?
questions.explanation: The Exclusive Legislative List contains matters on which only the National Assembly can legislate for the Federation. 'Defence' is one such matter. Agriculture is a concurrent matter, while chieftaincy and local government administration are not exclusive federal subjects.

questions.q: A state government establishes a university and makes laws for its funding, while the federal government also establishes a university in the same state and funds it through the National Universities Commission. This situation best illustrates the operation of
options: residual powers of the state government
exclusive federal powers over university education
delegated legislation by local government councils
concurrent legislative powers in the federal system
questions.explanation: Both the federal and state governments can legislate on education, so the existence of federal and state universities is an example of concurrent legislative powers. Exclusive powers would belong to the federal government alone, while residual powers are those left to the states outside the legislative lists. Delegated legislation refers to law-making by bodies to which the legislature has delegated authority.

questions.q: Which body is constitutionally empowered to make laws for the creation of new states in Nigeria?
options: The President, acting on the advice of the Council of State
questions.explanation: The National Assembly has the constitutional power to make the enabling law for creating a new state, subject to the required approvals and referendum. The President, INEC and the Governors' Forum may be involved in the process or in public discussion, but they do not make the law creating states.

questions.q: When the Nigeria Labour Congress calls out its members on a nationwide strike to press for a higher minimum wage, it is using the method of
questions.explanation: A nationwide strike is a form of direct action because the pressure group applies industrial pressure outside the normal legislative process. Lobbying would involve private persuasion of legislators, electioneering involves contesting for political power, and a referendum is a direct vote by the electorate.

questions.q: The July 1966 counter-coup in Nigeria brought which military officer to power as Head of State?
questions.explanation: The July 1966 counter-coup removed General Johnson Aguiyi-Ironsi and brought General Yakubu Gowon to power as Head of State. Murtala Muhammed and Olusegun Obasanjo later led Nigeria after separate military changes.

questions.q: Which Nigerian constitution first provided for a bicameral federal legislature?
questions.explanation: The 1954 Constitution introduced a federal legislature made up of a Senate and a House of Representatives, making it the first bicameral federal legislature in Nigeria. The 1922 and 1946 constitutions did not provide such a federal bicameral arrangement, and the 1951 Constitution had a central House of Representatives without a Senate.

questions.q: The Senate's confirmation of persons nominated by the President for ministerial appointments is an example of
questions.explanation: Confirmation of ministerial nominees by the Senate is part of the legislature's power to check and oversee the executive. Delegated legislation concerns regulations made under an enabling law, and judicial review concerns court scrutiny of laws or actions.

questions.q: In a federal system of government, powers are shared between the central government and the component units in a way that is usually set out in
questions.explanation: Federal systems divide powers between the central government and component units through a constitutional arrangement, which is normally contained in a written constitution. An annual budget, party manifesto or legislative resolution cannot create or define that fundamental division.

questions.q: Authority differs from power mainly because authority involves
options: a right to command that those subject to it accept as legitimate
the use of force to secure obedience
control over the means of production
questions.explanation: Authority is legitimate power: it involves a recognised right to command and a corresponding acceptance of that right by those subject to it. Power can be exercised through force or wealth without being accepted as rightful, so those alternatives describe power or influence rather than authority.

questions.q: Which of the following is a major agent in the formation of public opinion in Nigeria?
questions.explanation: The mass media are a major agent in forming public opinion because they circulate information, frame issues and provide platforms for public debate. The judiciary, armed forces and civil service are primarily institutions for adjudication, security and implementation rather than opinion formation.

questions.q: Which principal organ of the United Nations is responsible for approving the organization’s budget and apportioning its expenses among member states?
questions.explanation: Under the UN Charter, the General Assembly considers and approves the budget and apportions expenses among members. The Security Council deals primarily with peace and security, while the Economic and Social Council coordinates economic and social matters.

questions.q: One reason why some countries adopt proportional representation is that it
options: guarantees a single party an absolute majority in parliament
restricts voting only to members of political parties
enables parties to win seats in proportion to their share of the votes
avoids the need for coalition governments entirely
questions.explanation: Proportional representation seeks to translate each party's share of votes into a similar share of legislative seats. It may, however, make coalition governments more necessary rather than eliminating them.

questions.q: The appointment of Alhaji Musa from Kebbi State and other members drawn from different states into a federal board to reflect national spread best illustrates the principle of
questions.explanation: Federal character requires that appointments and public institutions reflect Nigeria's diverse states and groups. Separation of powers concerns the distribution of functions among the three arms of government, while federal supremacy concerns the hierarchy of laws.

questions.q: A military administrator in Sokoto State dissolves the elected local government councils and appoints sole administrators to run them. This action best illustrates that military rule
options: preserves the autonomy of local governments
strengthens the separation of powers between organs of government
replaces elected representative institutions with appointed officials
questions.explanation: Military administrations often suspended elected councils and governed through appointed officials, thereby reducing representative government. Preserving local autonomy, encouraging party competition and strengthening separation of powers are features associated with democratic civilian rule rather than the action described.

questions.q: The first Nigerian to serve as Governor-General was
questions.explanation: Nnamdi Azikiwe became Governor-General in 1960, representing the British monarch before Nigeria became a republic. Balewa was Prime Minister, while Awolowo and Bello were regional premiers.

questions.q: The National Judicial Council in Nigeria is chaired by the
options: Chief Judge of the Federal High Court
questions.explanation: The Chief Justice of Nigeria chairs the National Judicial Council, which handles matters affecting judicial appointments and discipline. The Attorney-General, Senate President and Chief Judge of the Federal High Court are not its chairman.

questions.q: The power granted by the Constitution to a Governor to pardon a convicted person is an example of
questions.explanation: The prerogative of mercy is an executive power to pardon or reduce punishment, although it is exercised under constitutional limits. It is not a court reviewing a law, the legislature delegating power, or a court following earlier decisions.

questions.q: When a trade union persuades the government to raise the minimum wage without the union holding any public office, this best illustrates
questions.explanation: Political power is the ability to influence government decisions and policies, even without holding office. It is not sovereignty, which concerns supreme legal authority in a state, nor legitimate authority, which is the accepted right to command obedience.

questions.q: In a confederal system of government, the central government
options: can abolish the governments of the component states at will
enjoys exclusive control over the armed forces of the component states
appoints the governors of all the component states
derives its powers from the component states and is relatively weak
questions.explanation: A confederation is formed by states that retain most sovereign powers and delegate limited authority to a weak central body. The central government cannot normally abolish state governments or appoint state governors at will.

questions.q: A radio station in Kano runs a phone-in programme where residents discuss the new water rate before the state assembly debates it. This best illustrates the role of the mass media in
options: shaping public opinion on government policy
questions.explanation: Mass media provide a platform for citizens to discuss and influence views on government policy, as shown by the phone-in programme on the water rate. They do not conduct elections, enforce laws or recruit party members.

questions.q: Which of the following countries is a permanent member of the United Nations Security Council?
questions.explanation: France is one of the five permanent members of the United Nations Security Council. India, Canada and Nigeria are member states of the United Nations but do not hold permanent seats on the Security Council.

questions.topic: Separation of powers and checks and balances
questions.q: The power of the President to return a bill to the National Assembly without signing it is an example of
questions.explanation: When the President withholds assent and returns a bill, the executive is checking the law-making work of the legislature. It is not legislative oversight, judicial review or delegation of legislative power.

questions.topic: Separation of powers and checks and balances
questions.q: Which of the following is a legislative check on the executive in Nigeria?
options: granting of pardon by the President
approval of the annual budget by the National Assembly
administration of oath by the Chief Justice
advice given by the Council of State
questions.explanation: The National Assembly checks the executive by approving or examining the annual budget before public funds can be spent. Granting pardons, administering oaths and advising the President are functions associated with the executive, judiciary and an advisory body, not a legislative check on the executive.

questions.q: Under a proportional representation electoral system, the number of seats won by a political party is determined mainly by
options: the size of its campaign fund
the number of candidates it nominates
the number of constituencies it can win
its share of the total votes cast
questions.explanation: Proportional representation allocates seats in relation to the proportion of total votes won by each party. The number of constituencies won is more relevant to first-past-the-post systems, while the number of candidates or campaign funds does not determine seat allocation.

questions.q: The primary consideration in the formulation of Nigeria’s foreign policy is the promotion of
options: the economic interests of developed countries
questions.explanation: National interest is the fundamental consideration that guides the formulation and execution of a country’s foreign policy. Foreign envoys, religious harmony and the economic interests of other states may affect particular decisions, but they are not the central consideration for Nigeria.

questions.q: Nigeria’s participation in the United Nations, the African Union and ECOWAS is best described as an example of
questions.explanation: Multilateral diplomacy involves a state dealing with several states or international organisations at the same time, as Nigeria does through the United Nations, the African Union and ECOWAS. Bilateral diplomacy involves relations between two states only, while isolationism and unilateralism are policies of withdrawal or acting alone.

questions.q: Nigeria’s intervention in the Liberian crisis through ECOMOG was principally intended to
options: restore peace and stability in the West African sub-region
spread Nigerian political parties to Liberia
secure a permanent seat on the United Nations Security Council
questions.explanation: Nigeria led ECOMOG’s intervention in Liberia mainly to restore peace and stability in the West African sub-region. The action was a peacekeeping and regional security effort rather than a means of securing a permanent Security Council seat, acquiring mineral resources or exporting Nigerian political parties.

questions.q: Judicial review means the power of the courts to
options: interpret the constitution and declare acts inconsistent with it void
make laws for the state in the absence of the legislature
appoint judges to the higher courts
approve the annual budget of the executive
questions.explanation: Judicial review is the power of the courts to interpret the constitution and to declare unconstitutional any acts or laws that conflict with its provisions. Courts do not make general laws, appoint all higher judges or approve the executive budget through judicial review.

questions.q: The law that principally provides for the functions and powers of local government councils in a state of Nigeria is made by the
questions.explanation: Under Nigeria’s federal system, the government of each state is required to ensure the existence of local government councils under a law that provides for their structure, finance and functions; such a law is made by the State House of Assembly. The National Assembly, Federal Executive Council and Council of State do not exercise that principal law-making role for local governments within a state.

questions.q: One major function of a political party in a democracy is to
options: present candidates for election and seek to control government
interpret the constitution and settle disputes
collect taxes and provide local services
questions.explanation: Political parties contest elections by presenting candidates and, if successful, seek to control or influence government according to their programmes. Conducting elections is the work of the electoral commission, interpreting the constitution is the work of the courts, and collecting taxes and providing local services are mainly functions of government agencies.

questions.q: Alhaji Bello, a resident of Enugu, obtains a court order requiring the Enugu State Government to repair a road it is legally obliged to maintain. This order is known as
questions.explanation: Mandamus is an order compelling a public authority to perform a public duty imposed by law. Certiorari is used to quash a decision, while habeas corpus concerns the release of a detained person.

questions.q: The type of authority that rests on long-established customs and traditions of a community is called
questions.explanation: Traditional authority is accepted because it is rooted in inherited custom and longstanding practice. Charismatic authority depends on personal qualities, while legal-rational authority rests on rules and office.

questions.q: A military administrator in Sokoto maintains obedience by imposing curfews and detaining opponents without trial. The type of power relied upon is best described as
questions.explanation: Coercive power is based on force or the threat of punishment, such as curfews and detention. Legitimate authority and traditional authority depend on acceptance of the ruler’s right to rule rather than fear of punishment.

questions.q: For a substantive resolution to be adopted by the United Nations Security Council, the vote must include
options: two-thirds of the General Assembly and the approval of the Secretary-General
nine affirmative votes and no negative vote by any of the five permanent members
a simple majority of all United Nations member states
seven affirmative votes, including at least three permanent members
questions.explanation: The Security Council has fifteen members; a substantive resolution needs at least nine affirmative votes and must not be opposed by any permanent member. The General Assembly's voting rules do not apply to substantive decisions of the Security Council.

questions.q: The Manufacturers Association of Nigeria presents a memorandum to the National Assembly proposing lower import duties on industrial raw materials. This action is best described as
questions.explanation: Lobbying involves direct communication with legislators or government officials in order to influence their decisions. Presenting a memorandum to the National Assembly is a clear example of such communication. Picketing, strike action and boycott are protest methods, usually intended to press demands through disruption or refusal to cooperate.

questions.q: When the President is accused of gross misconduct, the legislative process of removing him from office is called
questions.explanation: Impeachment is the constitutional process by which the legislature investigates and removes the President for gross misconduct. Recall is a process by which voters remove an elected representative, not a legislative trial of the President. A plebiscite or referendum is a direct vote by the people on an issue.

questions.q: Which statement is best illustrated by the fact that a state government in Nigeria cannot by itself sign a treaty with a foreign country, while only the federal government can?
options: Component states are sovereign entities recognised by international law
Component states exercise external sovereignty jointly with the federal government
Component states derive their powers directly from the United Nations Charter
The component states do not possess full external sovereignty
questions.explanation: Treaty-making and representation on the international plane belong to the federal government, so the states lack full external sovereignty. The states have internal autonomy, but they are not separate international persons, and their powers come from the Nigerian Constitution rather than the United Nations Charter.

questions.q: A country in which the president is elected for a fixed term and the office does not pass to an heir is best described as a
questions.explanation: A republic has a non-hereditary head of state, usually elected, who serves for a fixed term. Hereditary succession is a feature of monarchy, while theocracy refers to religious authority.

questions.q: Mr Kofi, a Ghanaian businessman resident in Enugu, applies to the President for a certificate conferring Nigerian citizenship after meeting the constitutional conditions. This process is known as
questions.explanation: Naturalisation is the legal process by which an alien acquires Nigerian citizenship after satisfying conditions set by law and receiving the President's certificate. Citizenship by birth or descent depends on parentage, while registration is reserved for special categories rather than ordinary adult aliens.
